HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN
CLINICAL COVERAGE CRITERIA
Spinal Surgery — Cervical Procedures
Document: CC-SPINE-2024 | Effective: January 1, 2024 | Replaces: CC-SPINE-2023

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
SECTION 1 — SCOPE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

This policy applies to all requests for cervical spinal surgical procedures
including but not limited to anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF),
cervical disc arthroplasty, posterior cervical decompression, and cervical
laminoplasty submitted for prior authorization review under HealthFirst PPO,
HMO, and EPO plan products.

CPT codes covered: 22551, 22552, 22554, 22600, 22610, 22612, 63045, 63048

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
SECTION 2 — MEDICAL NECESSITY CRITERIA
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Authorization for cervical spinal surgery (CPT 22551 and related codes) will
be approved when ALL of the following criteria are satisfied:

2.1 DIAGNOSIS REQUIREMENT
    Member must have a confirmed diagnosis of one of the following:
    (a) Cervical radiculopathy — nerve root compression with radicular symptoms
        (pain, numbness, weakness in dermatomal distribution)
    (b) Cervical myelopathy — spinal cord compression with myelopathic symptoms
        (gait disturbance, bilateral upper extremity weakness, hyperreflexia,
        positive Hoffman sign, bowel/bladder dysfunction)
    (c) Cervical disc herniation with objective neurological deficit

    Supporting documentation required: MRI or CT myelogram within 6 months of
    request demonstrating structural pathology consistent with symptoms.

2.2 CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT REQUIREMENT
    Member must have completed a documented course of conservative treatment
    prior to surgical authorization, consisting of ALL of the following:

    (a) Physical therapy: minimum 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy
        with documented functional outcomes. Therapy must be directed toward
        the cervical condition for which surgery is requested.

    (b) Pharmacotherapy: trial of at least two of the following for minimum
        4 weeks each:
        - NSAIDs or COX-2 inhibitors
        - Muscle relaxants
        - Neuropathic agents (gabapentin, pregabalin, duloxetine)
        - Oral corticosteroids

    (c) One of the following interventional treatments:
        - Cervical epidural steroid injection (minimum 1)
        - Cervical medial branch block
        - Trigger point injection series

    EXCEPTION 2.2(A) — MYELOPATHY PATHWAY:
    For members with confirmed cervical myelopathy (criterion 2.1(b)),
    the conservative treatment requirement is MODIFIED as follows:
    Physical therapy requirement is reduced to 4 weeks minimum.
    Interventional treatment requirement (2.2(c)) is WAIVED if treating
    physician documents that interventional treatment poses risk of
    neurological deterioration.
    Pharmacotherapy requirement (2.2(b)) remains in full.

    NOTE: The myelopathy exception applies only when myelopathy is the
    PRIMARY diagnosis. Cases where myelopathy is documented as a finding
    but radiculopathy is the primary complaint are subject to standard
    conservative treatment requirements.

2.3 IMAGING REQUIREMENT
    Current imaging (within 6 months) must demonstrate structural pathology
    consistent with the member's symptoms and proposed surgical level.
    Imaging must be interpreted by a radiologist or treating specialist.

2.4 PHYSICIAN DOCUMENTATION
    Treating physician must provide:
    (a) Attestation that conservative treatment has been completed
    (b) Clinical rationale for surgical intervention
    (c) Description of functional limitations
    (d) Statement of surgical risks and alternatives considered

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
SECTION 3 — EXCLUSIONS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Authorization will be DENIED when any of the following apply:

3.1 Surgery is requested solely for axial neck pain without documented
    radiculopathy or myelopathy.

3.2 Conservative treatment requirements have not been met as specified
    in Section 2.2, unless myelopathy exception applies.

3.3 Imaging does not demonstrate pathology at the proposed surgical level
    consistent with clinical presentation.

3.4 EXPERIMENTAL PROCEDURES: The following are considered investigational
    and are not covered under this policy:
    - Cervical disc arthroplasty at more than 2 levels
    - Cervical disc replacement combined with fusion at adjacent levels

3.5 PRIOR AUTHORIZATION EXPIRATION: Authorization is valid for 90 days
    from approval date. Procedures performed after expiration require
    new authorization.

4.1 Initial review: Performed by licensed clinician (RN or MD).

4.4 Appeal rights: Members have right to first-level appeal within 180 days

CALIFORNIA REGULATORY FRAMEWORK
Prior Authorization and Independent Medical Review
Relevant Provisions for Health Plan Appeal Determinations

Source: California Insurance Code (CIC); California Health & Safety Code (CHSC);

(CCR) Title 28.

Compiled for internal clinical review purposes. Effective dates as noted.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

PART I — INDEPENDENT MEDICAL REVIEW (IMR)
CHSC § 1374.30 et seq. | Effective: 1994, amended 2013, 2022

§ 1374.30 — RIGHT TO INDEPENDENT MEDICAL REVIEW
(a) Any enrollee whose request for a health care service has been denied,
modified, or delayed by a plan or its contracting provider on the basis of
medical necessity may submit an application to the Department for an
independent medical review of the decision.

(b) The right to IMR is independent of and in addition to any other
grievance process or appeal right. An enrollee need not exhaust the plan's
internal appeal process before requesting IMR, except as provided in
subdivision (c).

(c) EXCEPTION — URGENT/EXPEDITED CASES: For cases involving an imminent and
serious threat to the health of the patient, the enrollee may request
expedited IMR directly without first completing any internal appeal.

§ 1374.31 — PLAN OBLIGATIONS ON DENIAL
(a) When a plan issues a denial based on medical necessity, the plan SHALL:
    (1) Provide written notice of the denial within the timeframes specified
        in § 1367.01
    (2) Include in the denial notice: the specific criteria applied, the
        specific clinical reason for the denial, and notice of IMR rights
    (3) Provide the enrollee's treating provider with the same information
        within the same timeframe

(b) A denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied or
    the specific clinical reason for the denial is DEFECTIVE and shall be
    treated as if no denial was issued for purposes of appeal timelines.

§ 1374.32 — STANDARD OF REVIEW FOR IMR
(a) In conducting an IMR, the independent medical reviewer SHALL determine
    whether the health care service is medically necessary using the following
    standard:

    "Medically necessary" means health care services that a physician or other
    provider, exercising prudent clinical judgment, would provide to a patient
    for the purpose of preventing, evaluating, diagnosing, or treating an
    illness, injury, disease, or its symptoms, and that are:
    (1) In accordance with generally accepted standards of medical practice;
    (2) Clinically appropriate, in terms of type, frequency, extent, site,
        and duration, and considered effective for the patient's illness,
        injury, or disease;
    (3) Not primarily for the convenience of the patient, treating physician,
        or other provider; and
    (4) Not more costly than an alternative service or sequence of services
        at least as likely to produce equivalent therapeutic or diagnostic
        results.

(b) CRITICAL: The IMR standard does NOT require that the service be
    consistent with the plan's internal coverage criteria. If the service
    meets the standard in subdivision (a), the reviewer SHALL recommend
    approval regardless of whether the plan's internal criteria are more
    restrictive.

(c) The plan's internal medical necessity criteria may be used as a reference
    but SHALL NOT be the sole or determinative basis for an IMR decision.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

PART II — MYELOPATHY AND URGENT CONDITIONS
DMHC All-Plan Letter APL 22-014 | Issued: September 2022

Re: Prior Authorization Requirements for Time-Sensitive Neurological Conditions

The Department issues this guidance following review of denial patterns in
neurological cases across plan products.

II.1 — MYELOPATHY CLASSIFICATION
The Department has determined that cervical myelopathy with objective evidence
of cord compression and myelomalacia on MRI constitutes a condition with
potential for irreversible harm if untreated. Plans SHALL treat such cases as
urgent unless compelling clinical evidence supports otherwise.

II.2 — CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT EXCEPTIONS
For conditions where delay of treatment risks irreversible harm, plans SHALL
NOT require completion of a full course of conservative treatment as a
prerequisite to surgical authorization when:

(a) Objective imaging evidence demonstrates progressive pathology (cord signal
    change, myelomalacia, or progressive herniation on serial imaging), AND

(b) Treating physician provides documentation that conservative treatment has
    been attempted and has failed to arrest progression, AND

(c) Surgical intervention is indicated under generally accepted clinical
    guidelines for the condition.

The presence of myelomalacia on MRI is specifically identified as a finding
that may support waiver of standard conservative treatment requirements
even where a full course has not been completed, when the treating physician
documents urgency.

II.3 — PLAN CRITERIA VS. CLINICAL STANDARD
Plans shall not apply internal criteria that are more restrictive than
generally accepted standards of medical practice for conditions identified
in this guidance. Where a conflict exists between plan criteria and generally
accepted standards, the clinical standard governs.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

PART III — SPECIFIC PROVISIONS: PHYSICAL THERAPY REQUIREMENT
CIC § 10169.5 | Effective: January 1, 2023

§ 10169.5 — PHYSICAL THERAPY AS PREREQUISITE
(a) A health insurer or disability insurer shall not condition approval of
    a surgical procedure on completion of physical therapy where:

    (1) The member's treating physician has documented in writing that
        physical therapy is contraindicated or is unlikely to benefit
        the member given the nature and severity of the condition; OR

    (2) The member has completed a course of physical therapy and the
        treating physician documents that the member reached a functional
        plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms; OR

    (3) The condition involves objective evidence of structural neurological
        compromise that physical therapy cannot address.

(b) For purposes of this section, "functional plateau" means documented
    failure to achieve meaningful functional improvement after a course
    of therapy, as determined by the treating physical therapist or
    physician.

(c) A plan's internal requirement for a minimum number of weeks of physical
    therapy shall not be applied mechanically without reference to whether
    the member has achieved a functional plateau or whether the condition
    involves neurological urgency under subdivision (a)(3).

PART IV — TIMELINE REQUIREMENTS
CHSC § 1367.01 | CCR Title 28 § 1300.67.2.1

IV.1 — STANDARD PRIOR AUTHORIZATION
Plan must issue decision within:
- 5 business days of receipt of all information (standard)
- 72 hours for urgent/expedited requests

IV.2 — APPEAL DECISIONS
First-level internal appeal: decision within 30 days
Expedited appeal (urgent): decision within 72 hours
IMR determination: DMHC issues within 30 days (3 days for expedited)

IV.3 — DEEMED APPROVALS
If a plan fails to issue a decision within required timeframes, the
request is DEEMED APPROVED for the period of the delay.

PART V — INDEPENDENT MEDICAL REVIEW OUTCOMES (DMHC DATA)
Summary of IMR outcomes for spinal surgery cases, California 2023

Total cervical spine IMR cases reviewed:          847
Overturned (plan denial reversed):                612  (72.3%)
Upheld (plan denial confirmed):                   235  (27.7%)

Most common overturn reason:
  Conservative treatment already completed:       38%

    standard:                                     21%

the overall IMR overturn rate of 52% across all specialties, suggesting
systematic over-denial in this category.

CLINICAL REFERENCE SUMMARY
Cervical Myelopathy: Surgical Indications and Conservative Treatment Evidence
Compiled from published guidelines for utilization review purposes.

Sources:
- AANS/CNS Joint Section on Disorders of the Spine: Guidelines for Management
  of Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (2023 Update)
- North American Spine Society (NASS): Evidence-Based Clinical Guidelines (2020)
- AO Spine International: Clinical Practice Guideline (2021)
- Cochrane Review: Surgery vs Conservative Management for Cervical Myelopathy,
  Nikolaidis et al. (2021)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

SECTION 1 — DIAGNOSTIC CLASSIFICATION

1.1 CERVICAL MYELOPATHY vs. RADICULOPATHY — DISTINCTION

Cervical Radiculopathy:
- Compression of individual nerve root
- Unilateral or dermatomal symptoms
- Pain, sensory change, weakness in single nerve distribution
- Conservative treatment typically effective (70-80% resolution)

Cervical Myelopathy:
- Compression of spinal cord itself (not just nerve root)
- Bilateral symptoms common
- Upper motor neuron signs: hyperreflexia, Hoffman sign, clonus
- Gait disturbance, bilateral hand weakness, clumsiness
- Progressive course without treatment
- Conservative treatment has LIMITED efficacy for established myelopathy

CRITICAL DISTINCTION FOR TREATMENT DECISIONS:
Myelopathy and radiculopathy require fundamentally different treatment
algorithms. The evidence base for conservative treatment is primarily derived
from radiculopathy studies. Application of radiculopathy conservative
treatment requirements to myelopathy patients is NOT supported by clinical
evidence.

1.2 MYELOMALACIA — SIGNIFICANCE
Myelomalacia (T2 signal change within the spinal cord on MRI) indicates:
- Existing spinal cord injury/damage
- Higher risk of permanent deficit with continued compression
- Reduced likelihood of recovery even after successful decompression
- Surgical urgency — cord signal change is a predictor of poor outcome
  if surgery is delayed

Presence of myelomalacia on MRI is considered by major spine societies to
be a strong indication for surgical intervention and a contraindication to
extended conservative treatment trials.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

SECTION 2 — EVIDENCE ON CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT FOR MYELOPATHY

2.1 PHYSICAL THERAPY FOR MYELOPATHY
Evidence level: LOW to MODERATE

Key findings from Cochrane Review (2021):
- Physical therapy produces modest short-term pain reduction in mild
  cervical myelopathy (modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association score > 12)
- For moderate-severe myelopathy (mJOA score 8-12): physical therapy
  does NOT produce meaningful functional improvement
- For severe myelopathy (mJOA < 8): conservative treatment is NOT
  recommended as primary treatment

From NASS Guidelines (2020), Grade B Evidence:
"Conservative treatment may be considered for mild cervical myelopathy
as initial management, with close monitoring for progression. For
moderate to severe myelopathy, surgical decompression is recommended
as the primary treatment."

Critical quote from AO Spine Guidelines (2021):
"There is no high-quality evidence supporting a mandatory course of
physical therapy prior to surgical intervention for patients with
moderate to severe cervical myelopathy. Delaying surgery in such
patients to complete a physical therapy trial is not supported by
the evidence and may result in neurological deterioration."

2.2 CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT DURATION — EVIDENCE SUMMARY
For myelopathy specifically:
- No randomized controlled trials support a defined minimum duration
  of conservative treatment before surgery
- The 6-week PT requirement in many payer policies derives from
  radiculopathy evidence, NOT myelopathy evidence
- Applying radiculopathy-derived PT requirements to myelopathy patients
  is a category error not supported by evidence

2.3 RISK OF DELAY
From multiple prospective studies:
- Each month of delay in surgical treatment for moderate-severe myelopathy
  is associated with decreased likelihood of neurological recovery
- Myelomalacia on preoperative MRI is the strongest predictor of
  incomplete neurological recovery postoperatively

The HealthFirst Appeals and Grievances Department has completed its clinical and regulatory review of the first-level appeal submitted on November 5, 2024, regarding the prior authorization denial for a single-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C6-C7 (CPT 22551).

Accordingly, the initial denial issued on October 20, 2024, is OVERTURNED, and the procedure is APPROVED.

I. CLINICAL CASE SUMMARY
Mr. Thomas Reed is a 52-year-old male with a history of persistent, severe right-sided cervical radiculopathy. 
- Clinical Presentation & Exam: A neurological examination dated August 5, 2024, documented right C7 dermatomal distribution numbness, a diminished right triceps reflex, and a rest pain score of 7/10. No bilateral findings or upper motor neuron signs were present.
- Diagnostic Imaging: An MRI of the cervical spine dated August 1, 2024, demonstrated a C6-C7 disc herniation with mild cord contact (without measurable compression, cord signal change, or myelomalacia) and correlating mild right C7 foraminal stenosis.

  3. Interventional Treatment: Received a right C7 epidural steroid injection on September 20, 2024, which provided 30% temporary pain relief lasting 3 weeks before symptoms returned to baseline.

II. INITIAL DENIAL RATIONALE
The initial denial issued on October 20, 2024, by Dr. Patricia Huang, MD, cited reason code MED-003, stating: "Member does not meet criteria for ACDF. Imaging shows C6-C7 disc herniation with mild cord contact but no measurable compression. No myelopathy findings on exam. PT not yet completed to functional plateau."

III. ANALYSIS OF HEALTHFIRST CLINICAL COVERAGE CRITERIA (CC-SPINE-2024)
A review of the clinical record against HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024 demonstrates that Mr. Reed fully satisfies all requirements for the cervical radiculopathy pathway:

1. Diagnosis Requirement (Section 2.1):
   - Section 2.1(a) requires a confirmed diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy, defined as nerve root compression with radicular symptoms (pain, numbness, weakness in a dermatomal distribution), supported by an MRI within 6 months demonstrating structural pathology consistent with symptoms.
   - Clinical Alignment: Mr. Reed has a confirmed diagnosis of C6-C7 cervical radiculopathy. His MRI (August 1, 2024) shows a C6-C7 disc herniation and right C7 foraminal stenosis, which directly correlates with his documented right C7 dermatomal numbness and diminished right triceps reflex on physical exam (August 5, 2024). This satisfies Section 2.1(a).
   - Denial Error: The initial denial cited a lack of "measurable compression" and "no myelopathy findings." However, under CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.1, cervical radiculopathy (2.1(a)) and cervical myelopathy (2.1(b)) are distinct diagnostic pathways. Myelopathy findings and spinal cord compression are not required to satisfy the radiculopathy pathway. The reviewer incorrectly applied myelopathy criteria to a primary radiculopathy presentation.

2. Conservative Treatment Requirement (Section 2.2):

   - Clinical Alignment: The MRI dated August 1, 2024 (within 6 months of the November 5, 2024 appeal) demonstrates a C6-C7 disc herniation and right C7 foraminal stenosis, which is structurally consistent with the proposed C6-C7 surgical level and the patient's right C7 radicular symptoms. This satisfies Section 2.3.

4. Physician Documentation (Section 2.4):

The initial denial violates several key provisions of the California regulatory framework:

1. California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5 — Physical Therapy as a Prerequisite:
   - Under CIC § 10169.5(a)(2), a health plan shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on the completion of physical therapy where the member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating provider documents that the member reached a "functional plateau" without adequate resolution of symptoms.
   - Under CIC § 10169.5(b), "functional plateau" means a documented failure to achieve meaningful functional improvement, as determined by the treating physical therapist or physician.
   - Regulatory Noncompliance: The initial denial's insistence on further physical therapy despite the explicit PT discharge summary documenting a functional plateau violates CIC § 10169.5.

2. California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.32 — Standard of Review:
   - CHSC § 1374.32(a) defines medical necessity based on generally accepted standards of medical practice and clinical appropriateness. CHSC § 1374.32(b) explicitly states that the standard of review does not require consistency with the plan's internal coverage criteria if the service is clinically appropriate and meets generally accepted standards.
   - Regulatory Noncompliance: Denying a clinically indicated procedure based on an overly restrictive or misapplied internal criterion (applying myelopathy imaging thresholds to a radiculopathy patient) violates the statutory medical necessity standard.

V. ANALYSIS OF CLINICAL EVIDENCE AND GUIDELINES
Generally accepted clinical standards strongly support surgical intervention for this patient:

1. AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines for the Management of Cervical Spine Disorders (2023):
   - Under Tier 2 (Reasonable Indication), surgical decompression (ACDF) is recommended for patients with cervical radiculopathy who present with persistent, severe symptoms (pain score 7/10) and objective neurological deficits (diminished reflex, dermatomal numbness) that have failed to respond to an adequate course (6–12 weeks) of conservative therapy, provided there is clear structural correlation on imaging.
